Let’s wrap things up with Chapter 10: Sustaining Change—Mindset, Environment, and Self-Compassion.
Now, you've put in the work to make your home more functional and comfortable. But how do you keep that momentum going for the long haul? Well, it all comes down to your mindset, your environment, and, maybe most importantly, how kindly you treat yourself.
First off, let’s talk about perfectionism. It sneaks in when we least expect it, right? But your home doesn’t have to be perfect. Mess is going to pop up again, and that’s totally normal. The real goal is to have a space that supports your well-being and grows with you—even when life gets a little chaotic.
Here are a few principles that really help when it comes to sustaining change:
Make it a habit to check in on your routines and tweak them whenever life shifts. Maybe your schedule changes, or you pick up a new hobby—what works for you today might need a little adjustment tomorrow.
Arrange your space so good habits are easy. Keep things you use every day visible, and do your best to clear away anything that gets in the way. Little changes, like a basket by the door for outgoing items or a checklist on the fridge, can make routines almost automatic.
And—please don’t forget this part—practice self-compassion. If you hit a setback, see it as a chance to learn, not a reason to feel ashamed. We all stumble. What matters is that you keep going.
Visual reminders can make a huge difference. Maybe you hang a cheerful note near your workspace, or you leave supplies out where you can see them. These tiny nudges help turn new habits into second nature.
And don’t wait for some huge milestone to celebrate. Every bit of progress counts. Even on tough days, acknowledge the effort it takes to keep things in order. Sometimes, a small ritual—like lighting a candle after tidying up, or playing your favorite song while you clean—can turn chores into something you actually look forward to.
Most importantly, remember: your home is meant to be lived in, not put on display. Let it reflect who you are and what you need, not just what you think it’s “supposed” to look like. As your life changes, let your space evolve too. And give yourself permission to rest when you need it.
So here’s the key takeaway: sustaining change isn’t just a one-time thing. It’s an ongoing journey—one where flexibility, kindness, and adaptability matter way more than getting everything “just right.” When you nurture that mindset, you’ll find your home really can be a place that feels supportive and welcoming, no matter what life brings your way.
